text: When you type a message to an AI, like chat GPT, it doesn't process the sentence exactly
the way humans do.
Underneath the hood, the system splits your text into small, manageable pieces called
tokens.
Each of these tokens is assigned an embedding.
You can think of an embedding as a specific row of numbers that represents the token's
starting default meaning in isolation.
But words rarely exist in isolation.
The surrounding text, the context, shapes and determines what a specific word actually
means in practice.
This graphic displays two main problems context must solve.
On the left, problem one, different meanings.
Please turn on the light means brightness, but
the empty suitcase felt light means not heavy.
Moving to the right side, problem two, pronouns.
In the cat was thirsty, so it drank the milk, it refers to the cat.
In the milk was fresh, so the cat drank it, it points to the milk.
In both cases, context ultimately determines which meaning the AI must select.
As humans, our brains grasp the right meaning almost instantly,
just by taking in the surrounding words.
But for earlier AI systems, making these connections was a major mechanical hurdle.
Earlier AI read text sequentially, moving left to right, one word at a time.
Arriving at the pronoun it near the end of a passage,
the system often lost track of earlier words.
The connection back to cat was lost.
Because of this linear approach,
earlier models consistently failed to maintain conceptual connections
in anything longer than a brief sentence.
In 2017, researchers at Google published a paper called Attention is All You Need.
It introduced a new architecture called the transformer.
This structure became the foundation for large language models, and
it is the T in chat GPT.
Transformers read the same sentence differently.
The complete message arrives and is processed in parallel.
By seeing every word simultaneously,
the AI draws information directly from earlier words.
It instantly connects back to cat, skipping the words between them.
Receiving the complete message at once eliminates the barrier of distance
between connected concepts.
But simply seeing all the words is only the first step.
The AI must actively determine which surrounding words matter most,
and then use that data to update its mathematical understanding.
Two mechanisms do this work.
First, attention weighs relevant surrounding words,
drawing context from cat blending it into it.
Then transformation applies learned patterns to refine those numbers.
The data bars evolve into their final state with full context.
Attention and transformation are paired systems.
They work together continuously to synthesize the surrounding words into concrete meaning.
It is helpful to clarify exactly what is changing during this process.
The AI model's underlying learned weights are fixed and permanent.
What actually changes and updates is the specific row of numbers
representing the tokens in your current message.
These updates resolve our original problems.
On the left, turn on defines light as brightness,
while empty defines it as not heavy.
On the right, thirsty connects it back to the cat,
while fresh maps it to the milk.
Just as the word thirsty maps a pronoun to a cat,
evaluating how every word interacts with the rest of the sentence
allows the AI to map the complex relationships
that form sarcasm and idioms.
Ultimately, attention and transformation are the mechanisms
that decipher which intended meaning fits your prompt.
There is one final piece to this puzzle.
Having the right words is useless without the correct order.
The three tokens dog, bites, and man
create vastly different meanings depending on how they are arranged.
Transformers process everything in parallel,
naturally lacking a sense of sequence.
Without position information, words are just floating data.
The solution is positional encoding.
The system assigns a numerical position stamp to each token.
Dog is locked to position one,
bites to two, and man to three.
Positional encoding tracks the entire sequence,
telling the transformer exactly where every single token
belongs in the broader sentence.
This brings us back to the core mechanism
driving modern AI text comprehension.
As the researchers established, attention is all you need.
By mathematically mapping the intricate relationships
between words, AI successfully interprets your message.
